groups.name: Bacterial virulence factors
groups.explanation: These are all virulence factors that allow bacteria to invade and damage a host cell and organism.

groups.name: Lysosomal storage diseases
groups.explanation: Each of these are signs and symptoms of glycogen storage diseases

groups.name: Things that are "pin" related
groups.explanation: These four clues all have the word "pin" in common, either in their description, or in their names.

groups.name: Conditions of the CytoSKELETON
groups.explanation: Each of these slides or images could result from a mutation of a gene that contributes to the cytoskeleton

items.label: M
items.note: M protein is a virulence factor found in Strep pyogenes. It demonstrates molecular mimicry of the heart, and is involved in the pathogenesis of rheumatic fever.

items.label: A-B
items.note: A-B toxins are a type of multimeric exotoxin produced by bacteria. B stands for the binding subunit of the toxin allowing for intracellular entry. A stands for the action subunit, which promotes cellular injury.

items.label: Bacterial Endospore
items.note: Endospores are produced by some bacteria, allowing them to stay dormant and resist heat and chemicals. This is a Schaeffer-Fulton stain of Bacillus, and the arrow is pointing to the endospore, colored green..

items.label: DNAse
items.note: DNAses are a mechanism of bacterial immune evasion. They destroy neurophil extracellular traps (NETs), which are made mostly from neurophil DNA, which trap bacteria.

items.label: "Wrinkled tissue paper" macrophages
items.note: Gaucher cells have a characteristic "wrinkled tissue paper" appearance under the microscope

items.label: Cherry red macula
items.note: The cherry red macula is a sign of Tay-Sachs and Niemann-Pick diseases

items.label: Autosomal recessive
items.note: Lysosomal storage diseases typically follow an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern

items.label: Hepatosplenomegaly
items.note: Several lysosomal storage diseases can cause hepatosplenomegaly

items.label: Paresthesias
items.note: Paresthesias refer to a "pins and needles" sensation on the skin

items.label: Miosis
items.note: Miosis can also be referred to as "pinpoint pupils"

items.label: Petechiae
items.note: Petechiae are "pinpoint"-sized red, purple, or brown spots that are flat and painless

items.label: Spherocytes
items.note: This blood smear shows spherocytes that can be found in conditions such as Hereditary Spherocytosis or Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia. Hereditary Spherocytosis results from mutations in proteins such as ankyrin or spectrin which are found in the cytoskeleton.

items.label: WASp mutation
items.note: The WASp gene is mutated in the genetic conditions of Wiscott-Aldrich syndrome. The Wiscott-Aldrich protein regulates actin organization in the cytoskeleton. It is an X-linked condition that results in immunodeficiency as a result of impaired CD8+ T cell and NK cell function.

items.label: Situs inversus totalis (in Kartaganer syndrome)
items.note: Situs inversus totalis is total flipping of organs in the chest and abdomen. It can result from mutations in dynein protein which are an important motor proteins of the cytoskeleton causing Kartagener syndrome or PCD. Kartagener syndrome would show the flipped X-ray as shown.

items.label: Normal heart exam, infertility, and bronchiectasis.

info.title: Normal heart exam, infertility, and bronchiectasis.

items.note: Signs and symptoms of primary ciliary dyskinesia, which can result from mutations in cytoskeleton motor protein dynein. Unlike Kartagner syndrome the internal organs are not flipped.
